content.value_statement: Medical device teams face complex submission paths, quality requirements, and market access timelines. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code guide regulatory planning with structured MedTech expertise.
actual_capabilities: Develop regulatory strategy for FDA, EU MDR, ISO, and global market pathways.
Plan submission workflows from pre-submission consultation through approval monitoring.
Coordinate cross-functional regulatory activities across product, quality, clinical, and leadership teams.
Assess regulatory risks and propose mitigation steps for product lifecycle decisions.
Use included reference guides for FDA and EU MDR submission planning.
Track local submission status and deadlines with the included Python tracker.
limitations: It does not provide legal advice or replace qualified regulatory counsel.
It cannot submit documents to regulators or access authority portals.
It depends on users to verify current regulations and official guidance.
The local tracker is basic and does not integrate with enterprise regulatory systems.

use_cases.title: Define a market access path
use_cases.description: Map FDA, EU MDR, and global pathway options before product development decisions are locked.

use_cases.title: Prepare a submission plan
use_cases.description: Build checklists, timelines, and responsibility matrices for 510(k), PMA, De Novo, or CE submissions.

use_cases.title: Coordinate compliance readiness
use_cases.description: Align quality, clinical, engineering, and leadership teams around documentation and audit expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a regulatory pathway
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new device
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a regulatory pathway for a medical device. The device is [device type], the intended use is [intended use], and the target markets are [markets].

prompt_templates.title: Plan an FDA submission
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate 510(k), PMA, or De Novo preparation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an FDA submission plan for [device name]. Include pathway assumptions, required evidence, likely review steps, timeline risks, and cross-functional owners.

prompt_templates.title: Assess EU MDR readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our EU MDR readiness for a [device class] device. Focus on technical documentation, clinical evidence, QMS needs, UDI, and Notified Body engagement.

prompt_templates.title: Build a regulatory leadership plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as Head of Regulatory Affairs for our MedTech portfolio. Create a 90-day plan covering submissions, regulatory risks, team cadence, escalation paths, and executive reporting.

output_examples.input: Plan a 510(k) submission for a connected blood glucose monitor.
output: Recommended starting path: Class II 510(k) with predicate analysis.
Key evidence: analytical performance, clinical accuracy, software documentation, cybersecurity assessment, and labeling.
Core owners: regulatory, quality, clinical, engineering, software, and marketing.
Main risks: predicate mismatch, incomplete software documentation, and delayed performance testing.

output_examples.input: What should we prepare before contacting a Notified Body?
output: Confirm device classification and conformity assessment route.
Prepare a technical documentation gap analysis against EU MDR Annex II and Annex III.
Define clinical evidence strategy, PMS plan, PMCF needs, and UDI readiness.
Create an internal timeline that accounts for Notified Body capacity and review cycles.

output_examples.input: Create a regulatory risk review for an upcoming submission.
output: Market access risk: review delays from incomplete evidence packages.
Operational risk: unclear ownership across quality, clinical, and engineering teams.
Compliance risk: outdated guidance or insufficient post-market planning.
Mitigation: pre-submission engagement, responsibility matrix, and recurring regulatory intelligence checks.

best_practices: Start regulatory planning before major design decisions are finalized.
Validate assumptions against current official guidance and qualified experts.
Assign clear owners for evidence, quality records, labeling, and authority responses.
anti_patterns: Treating regulatory affairs as a final documentation step after development ends.
Using outdated pathway assumptions without checking current FDA or EU MDR guidance.
Relying on generic templates without adapting them to device class and intended use.

faq.question: What regulatory areas does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers FDA pathways, EU MDR planning, ISO-related readiness, global market access, and regulatory team coordination.

faq.question: Can it replace a regulatory consultant or lawyer?
faq.answer: No. It supports planning and analysis, but qualified professionals must review high-risk decisions and official submissions.

faq.question: Does it submit documents to FDA or EU authorities?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare plans, checklists, and communication strategy, but it does not access regulator systems.

faq.question: Which users benefit most from this skill?
faq.answer: Founders, regulatory affairs managers, quality leaders, and product teams working on HealthTech or MedTech products benefit most.

faq.question: Does it include operational tracking?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a simple local Python tracker for submission status, deadlines, overdue items, and status reports.

faq.question: How should users handle sensitive submission data?
faq.answer: Users should store sensitive data only in approved systems and avoid placing confidential records in unprotected local files.
